races.title: State Assembly, District 66
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Paul Seo
cands.bio: Mayor of Rancho Palos Verdes and a California Deputy Attorney General who prosecutes political corruption and white-collar crime. Former Los Angeles County deputy district attorney for seven years, U.S. Army officer and West Point graduate, with a law degree from Loyola Law School.

endorsements.text: California Professional Firefighters, Association for Los Angeles Deputy Sheriffs, United Nurses Associations of California, SEIU Local 99, California State Council of Laborers (LiUNA), SEIU 121RN, Planned Parenthood Advocacy Project LA County Action Fund and Sierra Club are listed on his campaign site.
Ballotpedia lists endorsements from California Environmental Voters and the Sierra Club Angeles Chapter, plus the Sway voting-group guides of Elizabeth Barcohana and Eric Say More.

cands.gaps: We could not find his birthplace or the year his family came to California. His campaign site gives no specifics on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buyers, H-1B or immigration enforcement, or gun policy. His housing and climate statements are general and could not be tied to specific growth or land-protection commitments. He has no state legislative record. His city council actions are described only on his own campaign site, with no independent reporting or council records. He did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 candidate survey. We found no news coverage of controversies.

local.label: Roots 90: His campaign biography says he was raised in Torrance by Korean immigrant parents who owned a local small business, and it does not give his birthplace.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Mayor and city councilmember in Rancho Palos Verdes, Deputy Attorney General leading corruption and fraud prosecutions, seven years as an L.A. County deputy district attorney, and a former U.S. Army officer.
qual.why: He has local elected office and a long legal career, which fits the middle band. He has no prior state legislative service and no documented budget-writing role, so he is not in the high band.
qual.label: He has local elected office and a long legal career, which fits the middle band. He has no prior state legislative service and no documented budget-writing role, so he is not in the high band.

back-police-order.evidence: Says that in the Assembly he will work to increase funding for more police, deputy sheriffs, prosecutors, peace officers and Highway Patrol officers, and to strengthen community policing.

pro-life.evidence: Says California must protect access to safe, legal abortion, and that he strongly supported Prop. 1 (2024), which put abortion rights in the state constitution.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: Says he will work with teachers to develop plans to increase pay for public educators. His site does not address vouchers, charters or school choice.

prio.label: Matches 2 of 3 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 2 only promised

roots.summary: His campaign biography says he was raised in Torrance by Korean immigrant parents who owned a local small business, and it does not give his birthplace.

cands.name: Sara Deen
cands.bio: Family dentist and co-owner of an urgent care clinic in Torrance. Elected to the Palos Verdes Peninsula Unified School District board in 2022 and now its president. Also sits on the SoCal ROC board. Democratic candidate for Assembly District 66 in 2026.

endorsements.text: California Teachers Association, California Nurses Association and National Union of Healthcare Workers (listed by Ballotpedia).

Her Ballotpedia survey also lists CA YIMBY, the California Dental Association, the California Medical Association, the California Federation of Teachers, the Democratic Legislative Women's Caucus, Indivisible South Bay LA, Western States Regional Council of Carpenters, and others. These are self-reported.

cands.gaps: We could not find where or when Sara Deen was born, or which city she grew up in. We found no independent reporting or official records confirming her school board claims, such as balanced budgets, the bond measure and the school safety framework. Those come only from her own campaign materials. We found no documented actions or stated positions from her on data centers, homestead property taxes, foreign or investor land purchases, immigration or H-1B, policing, gun laws, abortion, or school choice and vouchers. We found no news coverage of controversies, and no documented foreign ties.

local.label: Roots 90: Her campaign site says she grew up in California to immigrant parents and that her family settled in the South Bay in 2014; her birthplace is not stated.

land.label: 1 documented position for data centers or more development

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Palos Verdes school board member since 2022 and now its president; family dentist; co-owner of a Torrance urgent care clinic opened in 2023; previously taught in UCLA's Advanced Dentistry program.
qual.why: She holds local elected office (school board, including budget oversight) and owns a small business, which fits the middle band. She has no legislative or state-budget experience. Her SoCal ROC board seat and advisory board roles were not counted.
qual.label: She holds local elected office (school board, including budget oversight) and owns a small business, which fits the middle band. She has no legislative or state-budget experience. Her SoCal ROC board seat and advisory board roles were not counted.

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: Said in her Ballotpedia survey that she would streamline permitting and outdated regulations and expand starter homes and workforce housing, while keeping strong environmental and safety protections.

roots.summary: Her campaign site says she grew up in California to immigrant parents and that her family settled in the South Bay in 2014; her birthplace is not stated.

land_positions.quote_or_summary: Says she will "streamline permitting and outdated regulations, expand starter homes and workforce housing, support community land trusts" and help seniors downsize or repair homes. In another answer she says she would do this "while maintaining strong environmental and safety protections."
